      STIPULATION RE DEADLINE TO RESPOND TO COMPLAINT No. 3:26-cv-02409-AGT
      Case 3:26-cv-02409-EMC       Document 19     Filed 04/16/26   Page 2 of 5



 1         Plaintiffs and Defendants Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) and Luxottica of
 2   America Inc. (“Luxottica”), by and through their undersigned counsel, hereby agree
 3   and stipulate as follows:
 4         WHEREAS, Plaintiffs in the above-captioned case filed a putative class action
 5   Complaint on March 19, 2026;
 6         WHEREAS, Plaintiffs served a summons on both Meta and Luxottica on
 7   March 26, 2026;
 8         WHEREAS, Meta’s and Luxottica’s deadline to respond to the Complaint is
 9   April 16, 2026;
10         WHEREAS, Plaintiffs are in discussions with plaintiffs in other, related cases
11   about (i) consolidating those cases; (ii) application(s) for leadership; and (iii) the
12   timeline for filing a single consolidated putative class action complaint;
13         WHEREAS, those discussions remain ongoing;
14         WHEREAS, for the efficiency of the Court and the parties, Plaintiffs have
15   conferred with counsel for Meta and Luxottica, regarding the existing deadlines
16   including Meta’s and Luxottica’s deadline to respond to the Complaint;
17         WHEREAS, Plaintiffs, Meta, and Luxottica agree that the existing deadline
18   for Luxottica and Meta to respond to the Complaint should be stayed pending the
19   filing and outcome of those anticipated motion(s) for consolidation and application(s)
20   for leadership;
21         WHEREAS, this stipulation will not alter the date of any event or any deadline
22   already fixed by Court order;
23         NOW, THEREFORE, PLAINTIFFS AND DEFENDANTS META AND
24   LUXOTTICA HEREBY AGREE AND STIPULATE THAT:
25      • Luxottica’s and Meta’s deadline to respond to the Complaint is hereby stayed
26         pending a ruling on Plaintiffs’ anticipated motion(s) for consolidation and
27         application(s) for leadership.

        Case 3:26-cv-02409-EMC           Document 17         Filed 04/14/26      Page 3 of 3




 1           This matter comes before the Court on Plaintiff Peter Tittl’s (“Plaintiff Tittl”) Fourth

 2   Administrative Motion to Consider Whether Cases Should Be Related pursuant to Civ. L. R. 3-12 and

 3   7-11.

 4           The Court, having considered Plaintiff Tittl’s motion to relate Bartone et al. v. Meta Platforms,

 5   Inc. et al., No. 3:26-cv-01897-EMC (“Bartone”), Rowe v. Meta Platforms, Inc. et al., 3:26-cv-02398-

 6   JCS (“Rowe”) Rodgers v. Meta Platforms, Inc. et al., 3:26-cv-02401 (“Rodgers”) and Boylett v. Meta

 7   Platforms, Inc. et al., 3:26-cv-02409-AGT (“Boylett”) and good cause appearing, HEREBY GRANTS

 8   the motion.

 9           The Bartone, Rowe, Rodgers and Boylett actions concern substantially the same parties,

10   property, transactions or events, and it appears likely that there will be an unduly burdensome

11   duplication of labor or expense or conflicting results if the cases are conducted before different judges.

12   Therefore, the above matters are hereby related and reassigned to the undersigned judge.

13           SO ORDERED.

14

15   Dated: April 14, 2026
                                                   HON. EDWARD M. CHEN
16                                                 UNITED STATES DISTRICT JUDGE
